title: PostgreSQL Foreign Data Wrappers (postgres_fdw) and Pushdown
realWorldScenario: Your architecture team separates high-volume analytics into an isolated PostgreSQL cluster while user authentication lives in the core database. You need the analytics database to join `events` with `users` from the core database seamlessly.
questionStatement: Explain how PostgreSQL Foreign Data Wrappers (`postgres_fdw`) implement the SQL/MED standard. Detail the setup steps (`CREATE SERVER`, `CREATE USER MAPPING`, `IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA`). What is query pushdown (WHERE clauses, aggregates, joins), and how does network latency impact FDW performance?
expectedConcepts: CREATE SERVER, USER MAPPING, and IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA workflow
Predicate, aggregate, and sort pushdown to remote engine
Network round-trip latency and fetch_size parameter
hints: How does postgres_fdw avoid downloading the whole table when a WHERE clause is present?
What user mapping is required so the local user has rights on the remote server?
Consider the impact of network latency on joins between local and foreign tables.
